newsitem.title: FRANCE: RHONE-POULENC RORER LOVENOX GETS STUDY BOOST.
newsitem.headline: RHONE-POULENC RORER LOVENOX GETS STUDY BOOST.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc Rorer's anti-clotting drug Lovenox has been shown to significantly reduce the risk of death in patients treated for heart ailments, a study published in the New England Journal of Medicine said.

The study, published late on Wednesday, found that patients with unstable angina or a non Q-wave heart attack and who were treated with Lovenox, enoxaparin sodium, and aspirin had a significantly reduced risk of death than patients treated with unfractionated intravenous heparin and aspirin.
A Rorer official said in July the company expected sales of the leading Lovenox/Clexane drug to rise in 1997 to $475-500 million from $400 million in 1996.
The study was based on the ESSENCE trial, a prospective, randomized, double-blind, parallel group trial with 3,176 patients at 176 clinical centres in North and South America and Europe.

"Our study showed enoxaparin to be the first anti-thrombotic or clot-preventing agent proven superior to unfractionated heparin, which is the current standard of care in unstable angina treatment," ESSENCE study lead author Marc Cohen, director of the Cardiovascular Diseases and Catheterization Laboratories at Allegheny University Hospitals, was quoted as saying in the journal.
